comments.text: Living in Alaska completely redefines what human resilience actually means. Watching how the locals deal with endless frozen winters, months of dark polar nights, and extreme isolation with such calm acceptance is deeply humbling. It really makes you realize that living at the edge of the continent isn't a scenic holiday—it's a daily commitment to survival and preparation.

comments.text: In Skagway, grocery prices can be so steep that locals sometimes drive 2.5 hours into Canada just to shop at Walmart. For them, the long drive to Whitehorse is often cheaper than doing the weekly grocery run at home.
